finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: attacker-controlled req.body.callback is passed directly to axios.post with no URL validation, and the response status is returned to the caller.

trace.note: pub.post('/hooks/test') registered with no auth middleware
req.body.callback used as the POST URL with no scheme, host, IP, port, or redirect checks
r.status returned to requester, giving a status-code oracle

finding.guards_checked: None on the path: no auth, no scheme/host/IP allowlist or denylist, no private-range block, no port restriction, no redirect limit (axios follows redirects by default), no DNS pinning.

verdict.guard_found: none. routes.js:19 registers pub.post("/hooks/test") with no auth middleware. requireAdmin (routes.js:7-10) and admin.use (routes.js:12) apply only to the admin router, not pub. routes.js:20 passes req.body.callback straight to axios.post with no scheme, host, IP, or port check. No other files exist in the directory, so no app-level mounting or middleware was found.
verdict.reason: The source req.body.callback (routes.js:20) is attacker-controlled through the unauthenticated pub.post route (routes.js:19), and no validation exists before the axios.post sink (routes.js:20). One caveat: the candidate says the status is always returned, but axios throws on non-2xx by default, so the oracle is weaker than claimed. The app-level router mounting is not in the directory, so a global auth middleware cannot be ruled out, though none is visible.

finding.claim: SSRF via admin diagnostics endpoint: req.query.url is passed to axios.get with no URL validation, and the status is returned. Exploitation requires an admin session.

trace.note: admin.use(requireAdmin) applies the check to every route on the admin router

finding.guards_checked: Admin role check (requireAdmin, routes.js:7-12) is the only gate. No URL validation, redirect control, or private-address blocking. Severity lower than SSRF-1 because an admin session is required; mounting of the admin router was not visible in this directory.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only gate is requireAdmin (routes.js:7-10), applied to the whole admin router via admin.use (routes.js:12). No URL validation, hostname allowlist, or private-address blocking exists before axios.get at routes.js:15.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (routes.js:7, 12, 14-16 match the claims), but req.query.url at routes.js:15 is controlled only by a caller who already holds an admin session (routes.js:8, 12), which is not the unauthenticated or low-privilege remote attacker the source check requires, so the finding does not meet the bar for CONFIRMED. The admin-only SSRF is a real weakness that could be reported separately as lower severity, but not as this finding.
